metadata.title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Ramp Metering Based on Traffic Video Data
supplementary_materials: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.

hyperparameters.name: State matrix dimension
hyperparameters.context: Input size for the Q-network representing three consecutive frames.

hyperparameters.name: Replay buffer size B
hyperparameters.context: Capacity of the experience replay buffer for stabilizing training.

hyperparameters.name: Training steps T
hyperparameters.context: Number of decision time steps in one episode.

hyperparameters.name: Learning rate ̗
hyperparameters.context: Step size for the Adam optimizer during weights update.

hyperparameters.name: Batch size k
hyperparameters.context: Number of transitions sampled from replay buffer for each training step.

hyperparameters.name: Exploration rate ̵
hyperparameters.context: Probability of taking a random action in ̵-greedy strategy.

hyperparameters.name: Freeze interval F
hyperparameters.context: Frequency of updating the target network parameters.

hyperparameters.name: Decision step size L
hyperparameters.context: Fixed time interval between metering actions.

metadata.hardware_requirements: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)

nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Traffic volume and video data collected from the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao through a tunnel in Shandong, China, used for simulation calibration and DRL training.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Data available from the corresponding author upon request as stated in the Data Availability section.

nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations from raw images are extracted to reconstruct visual representations in the DRL method [24].
nodes_process.description: Extracts vehicle location points (xi, yi) from raw video frames to create position matrices mt. Includes down-sampling and stacking N consecutive matrices to represent traffic state st.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, generic tools used, matrix dimensions stated but extraction method refers to external work [24].

nodes_process.source_quote: The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1.
nodes_process.description: Trains a DRL agent using a revised Q-network with 3 CNN layers and FC layers. Employs experience replay, target networks, and a multitask learning strategy to predict speed and queue length.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all key hyperparameters and architecture details provided in Table 1 and Figure 7.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31].
nodes_process.description: Evaluates the trained model in 20 simulation experiments based on a real-world freeway segment. Compares performance against no-control and PI-ALINEA baselines.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, simulation environment and hardware are well-specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: Divides the control area into eight subareas and removes information from specific subareas to test the model's sensitivity to spatial data.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, subarea division is described in Figure 15, but exact data removal method is terse.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 8: Convergence curves for (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time.
nodes_sink.description: Convergence of the episode reward over 1 million training frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Training process and hyperparameters are detailed, but the specific random seeds for initialization are not provided.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 8: Convergence curves for (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time.
nodes_sink.description: Convergence of mean travel time (s) over 1 million training frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Methods are well-specified; minor gaps in exact initialization values.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Comparison of vehicle travel times (min) between no control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL across a 1-hour simulation period.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: SUMO simulator is open source and scenarios are well-defined, though raw traffic data is upon request.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Mean vehicle travel times (s) for 20 experiments comparing No controls, PI-ALINEA, and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear tabular results derived from specified simulation parameters and comparative methods.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Heatmaps showing speed distribution (m/s) over distance and time for (a) no-control, (b) PI-ALINEA, and (c) DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Standard spatio-temporal plots; derivable from simulation logs.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Queue length (m) at the on-ramp over time for three control scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Directly measurable outcome from the described simulation environment.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12: Relationship of queue length and red ratio for (a) PI-ALINEA and (b) DRL.
nodes_sink.description: Scatter plot and regression showing how queue length correlates with the signal red ratio.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Derived metrics from simulation; specific regression parameters not fully listed.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed
nodes_sink.description: Perturbation analysis showing travel time sensitivity to missing data in 8 different subareas.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Procedure for removing subarea data is clearly illustrated and results are logically presented.
